summary:
The starting-pitcher category is the story of the last two weeks: R1/R2 are both running 61% (106-68, n=174) with a +8.4pt spike over their season baseline, and R3 isn't far behind at 59% (102-72, +5.4pts). That heat lines up nicely with today's board, since seven of nine games carry full four-rating consensus, and the trends+sp combo remains the best pair in the shop at 57% (273-206, n=479). R3 is also the unit to trust with the wallet right now — 51-29 (64%, +24.0u) over the last 14 days on strong plays, and riding a hot 7-day stretch too (27-19, +7.0u), while R1 and R2 both bled cash in the last week (R1 -2.0u, R2 -5.0u) despite their better SP-specific numbers. That split matters: R1/R2 are the sharper SP-category tools, but R3/R4 are the better bets to actually cash strong plays today.

On the slate, MIL @ CHC is the biggest signal of the day — full consensus on MIL with R2's largest delta anywhere (-2.67), backed by a Henderson-over-Gausman lean, and MIL has been money when picked all year (33-18, 65%, strong 20-10 +11.0u). STL @ LAD is the second-strongest consensus, all four ratings on LAD by comfortable margins (+1.74 to +1.95), and LAD-when-picked is the single best team situation in the data set at 82% strong-play hit rate (+20.0u) — Skubal on the mound only reinforces a play the model already loves. BOS @ BAL is worth a flag: model likes BOS across the board, but modest at best (-0.34 to -0.68), and BAL-when-picked is a losing category (53%, strong 41%, -3.0u) — meaning fading BAL here fits the profile even though BAL isn't the pick. The two split games, MIA/KCR and TBR/TEX, are where confidence should drop hardest — R1 vs R2 disagree on MIA/KCR outright, and R3/R4 disagree with R1/R2 on TBR/TEX, so treat both as pass or small-stake spots rather than trend plays.
